items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: I remember being at one session, I didn’t play on it but I was lucky enough to be there, Machito’s band recorded in a huge hall

ctx.x: Yeah that’s a great way for a brass player to blow their chops trying to play over the — I don’t know if there’s any such thing as a pianissimo timbale.

No. And you’re right about brass players. It was a struggle. As a matter of fact nowadays I see how everybody’s got a microphone. You know those clip on mics that they have for the horns and all? So you get a good soundman who gets a good sound balance on it, you can hear everything clearly. That’s a pleasure. But although I should say that there was some great big band recordings done with, for example I remember being at one session, I didn’t play on it but I was lucky enough to be there, Machito’s band…

make that adjustment. But some of those albums sound great to this day, they really sound terrific. So technology offers the ability to do a lot of things that couldn’t be done, but that’s not to say that it’s better.
